objectives: Name the variable and the constants.
State a solution and check it.

sections.body: A linear equation in one variable can be written as ax + b = 0, where a and b are constants and a is not zero. The graph of a related function y = ax + b is a straight line.
sections.heading: Definition

sections.body: Undo addition or subtraction first, then multiplication or division. Apply the same operation to both sides. The solution is the value of x that makes the original equation true.
sections.heading: How a solution is found

sections.body: Solve 2x + 1 = 7. Subtract 1 from both sides to get 2x = 6. Divide both sides by 2. The solution is x = 3. Check: 2(3) + 1 = 7.
sections.heading: Worked example

sections.body: Terms used when this equation is discussed in English.
sections.heading: Technical terminology

terms.gloss: A symbol whose value is unknown until the equation is solved.
The steepness of the line; the coefficient of x in y = ax + b.
The y-value where the line crosses the y-axis.
